evidence.why: A complete chunk header updates the remaining byte count before payload extraction. When extraction returns None, the local chunk-start marker is lost before a later call emits Data.
Reader-instance state already persists chunk progress, footer consumption, and trailer processing across receive calls.
Existing public Connection coverage establishes the chunk-start and chunk-end semantics, but always supplies initial payload bytes with each nonempty chunk header.
The intact receive path translates a reader's None result into NEED_DATA without recreating the reader, allowing reader-instance metadata to survive fragmentation.

--- a/h11/tests/test_connection.py
+++ b/h11/tests/test_connection.py
@@ -266,7 +266,54 @@
     conn.receive_data(b"0\r\n\r\n")
     assert conn.next_event() == EndOfMessage()
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("header_separate", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("split_payload", [False, True])
+def test_chunk_boundaries_fragmented_header(
+    header_separate: bool, split_payload: bool
+) -> None:
+    conn = Connection(our_role=SERVER)
+    conn.receive_data(
+        b"POST / HTTP/1.1\r\n"
+        b"Host: example.com\r\n"
+        b"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n"
+    )
+    assert conn.next_event() == Request(
+        method="POST",
+        target="/",
+        headers=[("Host", "example.com"), ("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")],
+    )
+    assert conn.next_event() is NEED_DATA
+
+    for _ in range(2):
+        if header_separate:
+            conn.receive_data(b"5\r\n")
+            assert conn.next_event() is NEED_DATA
+            assert conn.next_event() is NEED_DATA
+        parts = [b"he", b"l", b"lo"] if split_payload else [b"hello"]
+        for index, part in enumerate(parts):
+            prefix = b"5\r\n" if index == 0 and not header_separate else b""
+            conn.receive_data(prefix + part)
+            assert conn.next_event() == Data(
+                data=part,
+                chunk_start=index == 0,
+                chunk_end=index == len(parts) - 1,
+            )
+            assert conn.next_event() is NEED_DATA
+
+        conn.receive_data(b"\r")
+        assert conn.next_event() is NEED_DATA
+        conn.receive_data(b"\n")
+        assert conn.next_event() is NEED_DATA
+
+    conn.receive_data(b"0\r\nX-Checksum: ok\r\n")
+    assert conn.next_event() is NEED_DATA
+    conn.receive_data(b"\r\n")
+    assert conn.next_event() == EndOfMessage(headers=[("X-Checksum", "ok")])
+    assert conn.their_state is DONE
+    assert conn.next_event() is NEED_DATA
+
+
 def test_client_talking_to_http10_server() -> None:
     c = Connection(CLIENT)
     c.send(Request(method="GET", target="/", headers=[("Host", "example.com")]))

spec.question: Receiving a chunked POST currently gives inconsistent boundary metadata: after processing the request headers, receiving b"5\r\n", calling next_event() until NEED_DATA, and then receiving b"hello" does not report the same chunk_start flag as receiving b"5\r\nhello" together. Fix receive-side chunk boundary reporting so the first Data event of every nonempty chunk has chunk_start=True, even when the chunk header arrives separately. If a payload spans several receive_data() calls, only its first Data event should have chunk_start=True and only its last should have chunk_end=True. Repeated next_event() calls while awaiting payload must not affect these markers. Preserve message completion and trailer handling. Return a unified diff against production files; leave tests unchanged.

suggestion.why_substantive: This exposes a distinct defect in the shown source: ChunkedReader records the parsed chunk size but keeps chunk_start only in a local variable. If the header arrives without payload, the call returns None and loses the start marker. Restoring reader-specific EOF dispatch cannot repair this behavior.
